title: In what order should these four numbers stand, smallest first?
description: Tanvi passes four villages on a school trip and reads the number of people on each board. The video sorts the numbers by digits first and then by place.
teaching_notes: One idea: sort by the number of digits first, then compare within a group. Watch for children who order by the first digit only.

video_script.why: The child can compare two numbers and now arranges four numbers of different lengths in order.
video_script.substitution: Group the numbers by digits, then compare inside a group from the left, and read from smallest to greatest.
video_script.anchor: boards in four villages on Tanvi's school trip showing how many people live there
video_script.wrong_answer: four thousand thirty five is the greatest
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu picks the number with the biggest first digit, four, as the greatest. One number has five digits, so it is greater than all the others.
video_script.payoff_line: three hundred forty five, three thousand four hundred fifty, four thousand thirty five, thirty four thousand five hundred

final_answer.spoken: three hundred forty five, three thousand four hundred fifty, four thousand thirty five, thirty four thousand five hundred

maths_rules: fewest digits is smallest: 345; most digits is greatest: 34,500
3,450 and 4,035 both have 4 digits; thousands digits 3 and 4; 3 < 4, so 3,450 < 4,035
slip: 4 is the biggest first digit, but 4,035 has only 4 digits and 34,500 has 5
your turn: 6,205, 620, 62,050; digits 4, 3, 5; order 620, 6,205, 62,050; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: group by digits, then compare. Wrong idea: the biggest first digit is the greatest. Four cards sit on the stage and are grouped by length.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Tanvi's class passes four villages on a school trip.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The first two boards show three thousand four hundred fifty and thirty four thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The other two show three hundred forty five and four thousand thirty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Arrange the four numbers in increasing order.

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: four cards appear in a row, one for each number; the digits on each card are counted by small ticks above it

marks.cards: four cards appear, one for each number
marks.tick: a small tick appears above each digit of each card

narration: <bookmark mark='cards'/>Write each number on its own card.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>Count the digits on every card.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Cards with the same number of digits can sit together.

marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Four is the biggest first digit, so four thousand thirty five is the greatest.
<bookmark mark='long'/>That looks only at the first digit, but one card is longer than all the others.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Count the digits before you look at any first digit.

beats.on_screen: the cards are grouped: 345 alone with 3 digits; 3,450 and 4,035 together with 4 digits; 34,500 alone with 5 digits

marks.group: the cards slide into groups by digit count
marks.small: the card 345 glows as the smallest
marks.big: the card 34,500 glows as the greatest
marks.mid: the cards 3,450 and 4,035 stay together in the middle

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Group the cards by their digits.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Three hundred forty five has three digits, so it is the smallest of the four.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Thirty four thousand five hundred has five digits, so it is the greatest.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Two cards have four digits, so they must be compared with each other.

beats.on_screen: the thousands digits 3 and 4 of the two middle cards glow; 3,450 moves left of 4,035; the four cards line up as 345, 3,450, 4,035, 34,500

marks.cmp: the thousands digits 3 and 4 of the middle cards glow
marks.read: the four cards line up from smallest to greatest

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Compare those two from the left. Their thousands digits are three and four.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Three is less than four, so three thousand four hundred fifty comes first.
<bookmark mark='read'/>Read the cards from smallest to greatest.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Three hundred forty five, three thousand four hundred fifty, four thousand thirty five, thirty four thousand five hundred.
